+"""Pydantic models for the Dev/SRE Toolbox API.
+
+These models define the wire contract only. The analysis logic lives in
+``app/toolbox/`` and does not import FastAPI or these models.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+Severity = Literal["info", "warning", "error"]
+
+
+class FindingLocation(BaseModel):
+    """Where a finding was observed. Fields are optional: not every tool has a
+    Kubernetes-shaped location."""
+
+    document_index: int | None = Field(default=None, description="Index of the YAML document (0-based).")
+    resource_kind: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Kubernetes kind, when applicable.")
+    resource_name: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Kubernetes resource name, when applicable.")
+    path: str = Field(default="", description="Dotted path inside the analysed document.")
+
+
+class Finding(BaseModel):
+    """One observation. A finding is never an HTTP error."""
+
+    code: str = Field(..., description="Stable machine-readable finding code.")
+    severity: Severity = Field(..., description="info | warning | error")
+    category: str = Field(
+        ...,
+        description="missing_configuration | risky_configuration | informational",
+    )
+    message: str = Field(..., description="Human-readable description.")
+    location: FindingLocation = Field(default_factory=FindingLocation)
+    suggestion: str | None = Field(default=None, description="Optional remediation hint.")
+
+
+class FindingSummary(BaseModel):
+    """Finding counts per severity."""
+
+    info: int = 0
+    warning: int = 0
+    error: int = 0
+
+
+class ToolRunRequest(BaseModel):
+    """Request body for POST /api/toolbox/runs."""
+
+    tool: str = Field(..., description="Identifier of the tool to run.")
+    input: dict[str, Any] = Field(
+        default_factory=dict,
+        description="Tool-specific input payload, validated against the tool's input schema.",
+    )
+
+
+class ToolRunResponse(BaseModel):
+    """Uniform result contract shared by every tool."""
+
+    run_id: str = Field(..., description="Correlation id for this run (response, logs, tracing).")
+    tool: str
+    tool_version: str
+    status: str = Field(..., description="Execution status: completed | failed.")
+    outcome: str = Field(..., description="Analysis outcome: pass | fail.")
+    summary: FindingSummary
+    findings: list[Finding] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    output: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    duration_ms: int
+
+
+class ToolCatalogEntry(BaseModel):
+    """One entry of the tool catalog."""
+
+    id: str
+    description: str
+    version: str
+    input_schema: dict[str, Any] = Field(..., description="JSON Schema of the tool input model.")
+
+
+class ToolCatalogResponse(BaseModel):
+    """Response body for GET /api/toolbox/tools."""
+
+    tools: list[ToolCatalogEntry] = Field(default_factory=list)

+"""Dev/SRE Toolbox router.
+
+Thin HTTP layer over ``app/toolbox``: it validates the request, resolves the
+tool from the explicit registry, dispatches the CPU-bound analysis to a worker
+thread (the same pattern ``/api/fib/{x}`` already uses) and maps the outcome to
+the documented result contract.
+
+Error mapping (kept deliberately distinct):
+
+* unknown tool id            -> 404 ``{"error": "Unknown tool", "detail": ...}``
+* tool input schema mismatch  -> 422 ``{"error": "Invalid tool input", ...}``
+* configured limit exceeded   -> 413 ``{"error": "Input exceeds limit", ...}``
+* run timeout                 -> 504 ``{"error": "Tool run timed out", ...}``
+* unexpected internal error   -> 500 ``{"error": "Internal server error", "detail": "run_id=..."}``
+
+404/413/504 are returned as explicit ``JSONResponse`` objects rather than raised,
+so the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them into the generic
+``{"error": "Bad request"}`` / ``{"error": "Not found"}`` envelopes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import time
+import uuid
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
+from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
+from loguru import logger
+from pydantic import ValidationError
+
+from app.auth import verify_credentials
+from app.config import get_settings
+from app.models.toolbox import (
+    Finding,
+    FindingLocation,
+    FindingSummary,
+    ToolCatalogEntry,
+    ToolCatalogResponse,
+    ToolRunRequest,
+    ToolRunResponse,
+)
+from app.toolbox.base import ToolInputError, ToolLimitExceeded, ToolLimits, summarize, outcome_for
+from app.toolbox.registry import get_tool, list_tools
+
+router = APIRouter(
+    prefix="/api/toolbox",
+    tags=["Toolbox"],
+    dependencies=[Depends(verify_credentials)],
+)
+
+
+def _effective_limits() -> ToolLimits:
+    """Resolve the configured limits for one run."""
+    settings = get_settings()
+    return ToolLimits(
+        max_input_bytes=settings.toolbox_max_input_bytes,
+        max_yaml_documents=settings.toolbox_max_yaml_documents,
+        max_yaml_depth=settings.toolbox_max_yaml_depth,
+        max_yaml_aliases=settings.toolbox_max_yaml_aliases,
+        max_findings=settings.toolbox_max_findings,
+        max_diff_context_lines=settings.toolbox_max_diff_context_lines,
+    )
+
+
+@router.get(
+    "/tools",
+    response_model=ToolCatalogResponse,
+    summary="List the available toolbox tools",
+)
+async def list_toolbox_tools() -> ToolCatalogResponse:
+    """Return identifier, description, version and input schema for every tool."""
+    entries = [
+        ToolCatalogEntry(
+            id=tool.id,
+            description=tool.description,
+            version=tool.version,
+            input_schema=tool.input_model.model_json_schema(),
+        )
+        for tool in list_tools()
+    ]
+    return ToolCatalogResponse(tools=entries)
+
+
+@router.post(
+    "/runs",
+    response_model=ToolRunResponse,
+    summary="Run one toolbox tool synchronously",
+    responses={
+        404: {"description": "Unknown tool"},
+        413: {"description": "Input exceeds a configured limit"},
+        422: {"description": "Tool input does not match the tool input schema"},
+        500: {"description": "Unexpected internal error"},
+        504: {"description": "Tool run timed out"},
+    },
+)
+async def run_toolbox_tool(request: ToolRunRequest):
+    """Run one tool. Findings are part of a 200 response, never an HTTP error."""
+    run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
+    settings = get_settings()
+
+    tool = get_tool(request.tool)
+    if tool is None:
+        logger.info("toolbox run rejected | run_id={} tool={} status=unknown_tool", run_id, request.tool)
+        return JSONResponse(
+            status_code=404,
+            content={"error": "Unknown tool", "detail": request.tool},
+        )
+
+    try:
+        payload = tool.input_model.model_validate(request.input)
+    except ValidationError as exc:
+        logger.info("toolbox run rejected | run_id={} tool={} status=invalid_input", run_id, tool.id)
+        return JSONResponse(
+            status_code=422,
+            content={
+                "error": "Invalid tool input",
+                "detail": [
+                    {"loc": list(err.get("loc", ())), "msg": err.get("msg", "invalid"), "type": err.get("type", "value_error")}
+                    for err in exc.errors()
+                ],
+            },
+        )
+
+    limits = _effective_limits()
+    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+    started = time.monotonic()
+
+    try:
+        result = await asyncio.wait_for(
+            loop.run_in_executor(None, tool.run, payload, limits),
+            timeout=settings.toolbox_run_timeout_seconds,
+        )
+    except ToolLimitExceeded as exc:
+        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
+        logger.info(
+            "toolbox run rejected | run_id={} tool={} status=limit_exceeded limit={} duration_ms={}",
+            run_id,
+            tool.id,
+            exc.limit,
+            duration_ms,
+        )
+        return JSONResponse(
+            status_code=413,
+            content={
+                "error": "Input exceeds limit",
+                "detail": f"{exc.limit}: {exc.observed} > {exc.maximum}",
+            },
+        )
+    except ToolInputError as exc:
+        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
+        logger.info(
+            "toolbox run failed | run_id={} tool={} status=failed outcome=fail duration_ms={}",
+            run_id,
+            tool.id,
+            duration_ms,
+        )
+        return ToolRunResponse(
+            run_id=run_id,
+            tool=tool.id,
+            tool_version=tool.version,
+            status="failed",
+            outcome="fail",
+            summary=FindingSummary(error=1),
+            findings=[
+                Finding(
+                    code="TOOL_INPUT_ERROR",
+                    severity="error",
+                    category="informational",
+                    message=str(exc),
+                    location=FindingLocation(path="input"),
+                    suggestion=None,
+                )
+            ],
+            output={},
+            duration_ms=duration_ms,
+        )
+    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
+        logger.warning(
+            "toolbox run timed out | run_id={} tool={} status=timeout duration_ms={}",
+            run_id,
+            tool.id,
+            duration_ms,
+        )
+        return JSONResponse(
+            status_code=504,
+            content={
+                "error": "Tool run timed out",
+                "detail": f"timeout_seconds: {settings.toolbox_run_timeout_seconds}",
+            },
+        )
+    except Exception:
+        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
+        # No traceback, no exception text: only the correlation id leaves the process.
+        logger.exception(
+            "toolbox run error | run_id={} tool={} status=error duration_ms={}",
+            run_id,
+            tool.id,
+            duration_ms,
+        )
+        return JSONResponse(
+            status_code=500,
+            content={"error": "Internal server error", "detail": f"run_id={run_id}"},
+        )
+
+    duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
+    summary = summarize(result.findings)
+    outcome = outcome_for(result.findings)
+
+    logger.info(
+        "toolbox run | run_id={} tool={} status={} outcome={} duration_ms={}",
+        run_id,
+        tool.id,
+        result.status,
+        outcome,
+        duration_ms,
+    )
+
+    return ToolRunResponse(
+        run_id=run_id,
+        tool=tool.id,
+        tool_version=tool.version,
+        status=result.status,
+        outcome=outcome,
+        summary=FindingSummary(**summary),
+        findings=[
+            Finding(
+                code=f.code,
+                severity=f.severity,
+                category=f.category,
+                message=f.message,
+                location=FindingLocation(**f.location),
+                suggestion=f.suggestion,
+            )
+            for f in result.findings
+        ],
+        output=result.output,
+        duration_ms=duration_ms,
+    )

+"""Core contracts for the Dev/SRE Toolbox.
+
+This module is pure Python: it does not import FastAPI, so every analysis
+function stays unit-testable and reusable outside the HTTP layer.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, Protocol
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+# --- Finding vocabulary -----------------------------------------------------
+SEVERITIES = ("info", "warning", "error")
+
+CATEGORY_MISSING = "missing_configuration"
+CATEGORY_RISKY = "risky_configuration"
+CATEGORY_INFO = "informational"
+
+
+class ToolInputError(Exception):
+    """Input is structurally valid but cannot be analysed by the tool."""
+
+
+class ToolLimitExceeded(Exception):
+    """A configured limit was exceeded.
+
+    Carries the limit name, the observed value and the configured maximum so the
+    router can return a controlled error that names the limit. Inputs are never
+    silently truncated.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, limit: str, observed: int, maximum: int) -> None:
+        self.limit = limit
+        self.observed = observed
+        self.maximum = maximum
+        super().__init__(f"{limit}: {observed} > {maximum}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ToolLimits:
+    """Effective limits for one run, resolved from Settings by the router."""
+
+    max_input_bytes: int
+    max_yaml_documents: int
+    max_yaml_depth: int
+    max_yaml_aliases: int
+    max_findings: int
+    max_diff_context_lines: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Finding:
+    """One observation produced by a tool. Never an HTTP error."""
+
+    code: str
+    severity: str
+    category: str
+    message: str
+    location: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    suggestion: str | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ToolResult:
+    """Tool output. ``status`` is the execution status, not the analysis outcome."""
+
+    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
+    output: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    status: str = "completed"
+
+
+def summarize(findings: list[Finding]) -> dict[str, int]:
+    """Count findings per severity. Deterministic."""
+    summary = {"info": 0, "warning": 0, "error": 0}
+    for finding in findings:
+        if finding.severity in summary:
+            summary[finding.severity] += 1
+    return summary
+
+
+def outcome_for(findings: list[Finding]) -> str:
+    """Analysis outcome: ``fail`` when any finding is a warning or an error.
+
+    ``info`` findings (for example "the two texts differ") do not fail a run.
+    """
+    return "fail" if any(f.severity in ("warning", "error") for f in findings) else "pass"
+
+
+class Tool(Protocol):
+    """Common interface implemented by every toolbox tool.
+
+    ``input_model`` is a Pydantic model used both to validate the request payload
+    and to publish the tool's input schema in the catalog.
+    """
+
+    id: str
+    version: str
+    description: str
+    input_model: type[BaseModel]
+
+    def run(self, payload: BaseModel, limits: ToolLimits) -> ToolResult:  # pragma: no cover - protocol
+        ...

+"""Explicit toolbox registry.
+
+No dynamic import, no ``eval``/``exec``, no shell: the set of runnable tools is
+fixed at import time and looked up by exact identifier. A duplicate identifier
+is a programming error and fails fast at import.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from app.toolbox.base import Tool
+from app.toolbox.tools.json_validate import JsonValidateTool
+from app.toolbox.tools.k8s_manifest import K8sManifestInspectTool
+from app.toolbox.tools.text_diff import TextDiffTool
+
+_TOOLS: dict[str, Tool] = {}
+
+
+def _register(tool: Tool) -> None:
+    if tool.id in _TOOLS:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Duplicate toolbox tool id: {tool.id}")
+    _TOOLS[tool.id] = tool
+
+
+for _tool in (JsonValidateTool(), TextDiffTool(), K8sManifestInspectTool()):
+    _register(_tool)
+
+
+def get_tool(tool_id: str) -> Tool | None:
+    """Return the tool registered under ``tool_id``, or None."""
+    return _TOOLS.get(tool_id)
+
+
+def list_tools() -> list[Tool]:
+    """Return the registered tools in registration order."""
+    return list(_TOOLS.values())

+"""json.validate — syntactic validation of inline JSON text.
+
+The tool only ever looks at the string it is given. It does not fetch URLs and
+does not read file paths: the input schema has a single free-text field, so
+nothing is dereferenced.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from app.toolbox.base import (
+    CATEGORY_INFO,
+    Finding,
+    ToolLimitExceeded,
+    ToolLimits,
+    ToolResult,
+)
+
+
+class JsonValidateInput(BaseModel):
+    """Input schema for json.validate."""
+
+    text: str = Field(
+        ...,
+        description=(
+            "Inline JSON text to validate. URLs and file paths are not accepted: "
+            "the value is parsed as-is and never dereferenced."
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+class JsonValidateTool:
+    """Check that a string is syntactically valid JSON."""
+
+    id = "json.validate"
+    version = "1.0.0"
+    description = (
+        "Validate inline JSON text. Returns the parsed value, or a syntax error "
+        "with its position when available. URLs and file paths are not accepted."
+    )
+    input_model = JsonValidateInput
+
+    def run(self, payload: JsonValidateInput, limits: ToolLimits) -> ToolResult:
+        text = payload.text
+
+        size = len(text.encode("utf-8"))
+        if size > limits.max_input_bytes:
+            raise ToolLimitExceeded("max_input_bytes", size, limits.max_input_bytes)
+
+        if not text.strip():
+            return ToolResult(
+                findings=[
+                    Finding(
+                        code="JSON_EMPTY_INPUT",
+                        severity="error",
+                        category=CATEGORY_INFO,
+                        message="Input is empty or whitespace only.",
+                        location={"path": "text"},
+                        suggestion="Provide a JSON document to validate.",
+                    )
+                ],
+                output={"valid": False},
+            )
+
+        try:
+            value = json.loads(text)
+        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
+            return ToolResult(
+                findings=[
+                    Finding(
+                        code="JSON_INVALID_SYNTAX",
+                        severity="error",
+                        category=CATEGORY_INFO,
+                        message=f"Invalid JSON: {exc.msg}",
+                        location={"path": f"line {exc.lineno} column {exc.colno} (char {exc.pos})"},
+                        suggestion="Fix the syntax at the reported position and retry.",
+                    )
+                ],
+                output={"valid": False},
+            )
+
+        return ToolResult(findings=[], output={"valid": True, "value": value})

+"""k8s.manifest.inspect — static, offline checks on Kubernetes YAML manifests.
+
+Scope and honesty of the checks
+-------------------------------
+These are heuristic static checks over the manifest text that was supplied.
+They are **neither a complete Kubernetes validation nor a security
+certification**: no API server, no admission controller, no policy engine and no
+cluster state is consulted. Only Deployment, StatefulSet and DaemonSet are
+inspected in this MVP.
+
+Safety
+------
+* YAML is parsed with a ``yaml.SafeLoader`` subclass, so no arbitrary Python
+  object is ever constructed.
+* The loader enforces a composition-depth budget and an alias/anchor budget
+  *during* composition, so a deeply nested or anchor-amplified document is
+  rejected before it can be materialised.
+* The composed object graph is walked again with a cycle-aware depth guard, so
+  a self-referential anchor cannot cause an unbounded traversal.
+* Input size, document count and finding count are bounded; exceeding any of
+  them raises ``ToolLimitExceeded`` (a controlled error, never a truncation).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from functools import partial
+from typing import Any
+
+import yaml
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from app.toolbox.base import (
+    CATEGORY_INFO,
+    CATEGORY_MISSING,
+    CATEGORY_RISKY,
+    Finding,
+    ToolLimitExceeded,
+    ToolLimits,
+    ToolResult,
+)
+
+DISCLAIMER = (
+    "Heuristic static checks on the supplied manifest only. This is neither a "
+    "complete Kubernetes validation nor a security certification."
+)
+
+SUPPORTED_KINDS = ("Deployment", "StatefulSet", "DaemonSet")
+
+
+class K8sManifestInput(BaseModel):
+    """Input schema for k8s.manifest.inspect."""
+
+    manifest: str = Field(
+        ...,
+        description="Kubernetes YAML manifest, possibly containing multiple documents.",
+    )
+
+
+class _BoundedSafeLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
+    """SafeLoader with a composition-depth budget and an alias budget."""
+
+    def __init__(self, stream: Any, *, max_depth: int, max_aliases: int) -> None:
+        super().__init__(stream)
+        self._max_depth = max_depth
+        self._max_aliases = max_aliases
+        self._depth = 0
+        self._aliases = 0
+
+    def compose_node(self, parent: Any, index: Any) -> Any:
+        if self.check_event(yaml.AliasEvent):
+            self._aliases += 1
+            if self._aliases > self._max_aliases:
+                raise ToolLimitExceeded("max_yaml_aliases", self._aliases, self._max_aliases)
+        self._depth += 1
+        try:
+            if self._depth > self._max_depth:
+                raise ToolLimitExceeded("max_yaml_depth", self._depth, self._max_depth)
+            return super().compose_node(parent, index)
+        finally:
+            self._depth -= 1
+
+
+def _assert_object_depth(obj: Any, max_depth: int) -> None:
+    """Cycle-aware depth guard over the composed object graph."""
+    seen: set[int] = set()
+
+    def walk(node: Any, depth: int) -> None:
+        if depth > max_depth:
+            raise ToolLimitExceeded("max_yaml_depth", depth, max_depth)
+        if isinstance(node, dict):
+            if id(node) in seen:
+                return
+            seen.add(id(node))
+            for value in node.values():
+                walk(value, depth + 1)
+        elif isinstance(node, list):
+            if id(node) in seen:
+                return
+            seen.add(id(node))
+            for value in node:
+                walk(value, depth + 1)
+
+    walk(obj, 0)
+
+
+def _yaml_error_message(exc: yaml.YAMLError) -> str:
+    """Report the problem and its position without echoing the source line."""
+    problem = getattr(exc, "problem", None) or "syntax error"
+    mark = getattr(exc, "problem_mark", None)
+    if mark is not None:
+        return f"{problem} (line {mark.line + 1}, column {mark.column + 1})"
+    return str(problem)
+
+
+def _finding(
+    code: str,
+    severity: str,
+    category: str,
+    message: str,
+    *,
+    document_index: int | None,
+    kind: str | None,
+    name: str | None,
+    path: str,
+    suggestion: str | None = None,
+) -> Finding:
+    return Finding(
+        code=code,
+        severity=severity,
+        category=category,
+        message=message,
+        location={
+            "document_index": document_index,
+            "resource_kind": kind,
+            "resource_name": name,
+            "path": path,
+        },
+        suggestion=suggestion,
+    )
+
+
+def _image_findings(
+    image: Any,
+    *,
+    document_index: int,
+    kind: str,
+    name: str | None,
+    path: str,
+) -> list[Finding]:
+    if not isinstance(image, str) or not image.strip():
+        return [
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_IMAGE_MISSING",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                "Container does not declare an image.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=path,
+                suggestion="Pin an explicit image reference.",
+            )
+        ]
+
+    # Digest reference (image@sha256:...) is immutable: nothing to report.
+    if "@" in image:
+        return []
+
+    last_segment = image.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+    if ":" in last_segment:
+        tag = last_segment.rsplit(":", 1)[1]
+        if tag == "latest":
+            return [
+                _finding(
+                    "K8S_IMAGE_LATEST_TAG",
+                    "warning",
+                    CATEGORY_RISKY,
+                    f"Image '{image}' uses the mutable 'latest' tag.",
+                    document_index=document_index,
+                    kind=kind,
+                    name=name,
+                    path=path,
+                    suggestion="Pin an immutable tag or a digest.",
+                )
+            ]
+        return []
+
+    return [
+        _finding(
+            "K8S_IMAGE_NO_TAG",
+            "warning",
+            CATEGORY_RISKY,
+            f"Image '{image}' has no tag and implicitly resolves to 'latest'.",
+            document_index=document_index,
+            kind=kind,
+            name=name,
+            path=path,
+            suggestion="Pin an immutable tag or a digest.",
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def _container_findings(
+    container: dict[str, Any],
+    index: int,
+    *,
+    document_index: int,
+    kind: str,
+    name: str | None,
+    base_path: str,
+    is_init: bool,
+    pod_security_context: dict[str, Any],
+) -> list[Finding]:
+    findings: list[Finding] = []
+    container_path = f"{base_path}[{index}]"
+    raw_name = container.get("name")
+    container_name = raw_name if isinstance(raw_name, str) else f"#{index}"
+    label = "Init container" if is_init else "Container"
+
+    # --- resources: missing configuration ---
+    resources = container.get("resources")
+    if not isinstance(resources, dict):
+        resources = {}
+    if not resources.get("requests"):
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_REQUESTS",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' does not declare resource requests.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.resources.requests",
+                suggestion="Declare CPU/memory requests so the scheduler can place the pod.",
+            )
+        )
+    if not resources.get("limits"):
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_LIMITS",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' does not declare resource limits.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.resources.limits",
+                suggestion="Declare CPU/memory limits to bound the container.",
+            )
+        )
+
+    # --- probes: regular containers only, init containers run to completion ---
+    if not is_init:
+        if not container.get("readinessProbe"):
+            findings.append(
+                _finding(
+                    "K8S_MISSING_READINESS_PROBE",
+                    "warning",
+                    CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                    f"Container '{container_name}' has no readinessProbe.",
+                    document_index=document_index,
+                    kind=kind,
+                    name=name,
+                    path=f"{container_path}.readinessProbe",
+                    suggestion="Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches ready pods.",
+                )
+            )
+        if not container.get("livenessProbe"):
+            findings.append(
+                _finding(
+                    "K8S_MISSING_LIVENESS_PROBE",
+                    "warning",
+                    CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                    f"Container '{container_name}' has no livenessProbe.",
+                    document_index=document_index,
+                    kind=kind,
+                    name=name,
+                    path=f"{container_path}.livenessProbe",
+                    suggestion="Add a livenessProbe so a stuck container is restarted.",
+                )
+            )
+
+    # --- image ---
+    findings.extend(
+        _image_findings(
+            container.get("image"),
+            document_index=document_index,
+            kind=kind,
+            name=name,
+            path=f"{container_path}.image",
+        )
+    )
+
+    # --- securityContext ---
+    security_context = container.get("securityContext")
+    if not isinstance(security_context, dict):
+        security_context = {}
+
+    if security_context.get("privileged") is True:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER",
+                "error",
+                CATEGORY_RISKY,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' is configured as privileged.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.securityContext.privileged",
+                suggestion="Disable privileged unless explicitly needed.",
+            )
+        )
+
+    allow_escalation = security_context.get("allowPrivilegeEscalation")
+    if allow_escalation is True:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_ENABLED",
+                "error",
+                CATEGORY_RISKY,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' explicitly allows privilege escalation.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation",
+                suggestion="Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.",
+            )
+        )
+    elif allow_escalation is not False:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_NOT_DISABLED",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' does not explicitly disable privilege escalation.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation",
+                suggestion="Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false explicitly.",
+            )
+        )
+
+    # --- non-root: container level wins over pod level ---
+    container_non_root = security_context.get("runAsNonRoot")
+    pod_non_root = pod_security_context.get("runAsNonRoot")
+    effective_non_root = container_non_root if container_non_root is not None else pod_non_root
+    if effective_non_root is False:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_RUN_AS_ROOT_ALLOWED",
+                "error",
+                CATEGORY_RISKY,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' explicitly allows running as root.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.securityContext.runAsNonRoot",
+                suggestion="Set runAsNonRoot: true at pod or container level.",
+            )
+        )
+    elif effective_non_root is not True:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_RUN_AS_NON_ROOT_NOT_REQUIRED",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_MISSING,
+                f"{label} '{container_name}' does not require non-root execution.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=kind,
+                name=name,
+                path=f"{container_path}.securityContext.runAsNonRoot",
+                suggestion="Set runAsNonRoot: true at pod or container level.",
+            )
+        )
+
+    return findings
+
+
+def _inspect_document(
+    doc: Any, document_index: int
+) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, Any] | None, int]:
+    """Inspect one YAML document. Returns (findings, inspected_entry, containers_checked)."""
+    findings: list[Finding] = []
+
+    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_DOCUMENT_NOT_MAPPING",
+                "warning",
+                CATEGORY_INFO,
+                "Document is not a YAML mapping and was skipped.",
+                document_index=document_index,
+                kind=None,
+                name=None,
+                path="",
+                suggestion="Provide a Kubernetes resource mapping.",
+            )
+        )
+        return findings, None, 0
+
+    kind = doc.get("kind")
+    metadata = doc.get("metadata")
+    name = metadata.get("name") if isinstance(metadata, dict) and isinstance(metadata.get("name"), str) else None
+
+    if kind not in SUPPORTED_KINDS:
+        findings.append(
+            _finding(
+                "K8S_UNSUPPORTED_KIND",
+                "info",
+                CATEGORY_INFO,
+                f"Resource kind '{kind}' is not inspected by this tool.",

+"""text.diff — unified diff between two inline strings."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import difflib
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from app.toolbox.base import (
+    CATEGORY_INFO,
+    Finding,
+    ToolLimitExceeded,
+    ToolLimits,
+    ToolResult,
+)
+
+# Hard schema bound. The effective cap is also configurable through
+# TOOLBOX_MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES and enforced again in run().
+MAX_CONTEXT_LINES = 50
+
+
+class TextDiffInput(BaseModel):
+    """Input schema for text.diff."""
+
+    left: str = Field(..., description="Original text.")
+    right: str = Field(..., description="Modified text.")
+    context_lines: int = Field(
+        default=3,
+        ge=0,
+        le=MAX_CONTEXT_LINES,
+        description=f"Context lines around each change (0-{MAX_CONTEXT_LINES}).",
+    )
+
+
+class TextDiffTool:
+    """Return a unified diff between two strings."""
+
+    id = "text.diff"
+    version = "1.0.0"
+    description = (
+        "Return a unified diff between two inline strings, with a configurable "
+        "number of context lines."
+    )
+    input_model = TextDiffInput
+
+    def run(self, payload: TextDiffInput, limits: ToolLimits) -> ToolResult:
+        if payload.context_lines > limits.max_diff_context_lines:
+            raise ToolLimitExceeded(
+                "max_diff_context_lines",
+                payload.context_lines,
+                limits.max_diff_context_lines,
+            )
+
+        size = len(payload.left.encode("utf-8")) + len(payload.right.encode("utf-8"))
+        if size > limits.max_input_bytes:
+            raise ToolLimitExceeded("max_input_bytes", size, limits.max_input_bytes)
+
+        diff_lines = list(
+            difflib.unified_diff(
+                payload.left.splitlines(),
+                payload.right.splitlines(),
+                fromfile="left",
+                tofile="right",
+                n=payload.context_lines,
+                lineterm="",
+            )
+        )
+        identical = not diff_lines
+        added = sum(1 for line in diff_lines if line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"))
+        removed = sum(1 for line in diff_lines if line.startswith("-") and not line.startswith("---"))
+
+        findings: list[Finding] = []
+        if not identical:
+            findings.append(
+                Finding(
+                    code="TEXT_DIFF_DIFFERENT",
+                    severity="info",
+                    category=CATEGORY_INFO,
+                    message="The two inputs differ.",
+                    location={"path": "left/right"},
+                    suggestion=None,
+                )
+            )
+
+        return ToolResult(
+            findings=findings,
+            output={
+                "identical": identical,
+                "diff": "\n".join(diff_lines),
+                "added_lines": added,
+                "removed_lines": removed,
+            },
+        )

+# 14 — Dev/SRE Toolbox
+
+**Status:** implemented (MVP). **Audience:** developers, SRE, security.
+
+## Explanation — what the feature is
+
+The Dev/SRE Toolbox is a small, self-contained catalog of technical utilities that
+developers and SREs run through the existing API and that return a structured
+result. It is deliberately **not** a new service and **not** a rewrite: it is a
+package (`app/toolbox/`) plus one router (`app/routers/toolbox.py`) mounted by the
+existing `create_app()` factory in `app/main.py`.
+
+Three tools ship in this MVP:
+
+| Tool id | Purpose |
+|---------|---------|
+| `json.validate` | Check that inline JSON text is syntactically valid; return the parsed value, or a syntax error with its position when available. |
+| `text.diff` | Return a unified diff between two inline strings, with a configurable number of context lines. |
+| `k8s.manifest.inspect` | Static, offline checks on Kubernetes YAML manifests (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet). |
+
+### The result contract
+
+Every run returns the same shape, regardless of the tool:
+
+
+{
+  "run_id": "uuid",
+  "tool": "k8s.manifest.inspect",
+  "tool_version": "1.0.0",
+  "status": "completed",
+  "outcome": "fail",
+  "summary": {"info": 0, "warning": 2, "error": 1},
+  "findings": [
+    {
+      "code": "K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER",
+      "severity": "error",
+      "category": "risky_configuration",
+      "message": "Container 'app' is configured as privileged.",
+      "location": {
+        "document_index": 0,
+        "resource_kind": "Deployment",
+        "resource_name": "example",
+        "path": "spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.privileged"
+      },
+      "suggestion": "Disable privileged unless explicitly needed."
+    }
+  ],
+  "output": {},
+  "duration_ms": 12
+}
+
+
+Four concepts are kept strictly distinct:
+
+| Concept | Where it lives | Example |
+|---------|----------------|---------|
+| Execution status | `status` | `completed`, `failed` |
+| Analysis outcome | `outcome` | `pass`, `fail` |
+| Request validation error | HTTP 422 | malformed body, or payload that does not match the tool input schema |
+| Unexpected internal error | HTTP 500 | sanitized body carrying only `run_id` |
+
+A **finding is never an HTTP error**. A manifest with a privileged container is a
+successful run (`status: completed`) whose analysis outcome is `fail`. Likewise,
+syntactically invalid JSON or YAML is a *negative analysis result* (a finding),
+not an HTTP error, because detecting that is the tool's purpose.
+
+`run_id` is a correlation id only: it appears in the response, in the structured
+log line and (when tracing is enabled) in the span. There is no run persistence
+and no `GET /runs/{id}`.
+
+## Tutorial — running the tools
+
+All toolbox endpoints require the same Basic Auth as `/api/debug/*` and
+`/api/mcp` (`DIAG_USERNAME` / `DIAG_PASSWORD`).
+
+### List the catalog
+
+bash
+curl -s -u admin:password http://localhost:8000/api/toolbox/tools | python3 -m json.tool
+
+
+### Validate JSON
+
+bash
+curl -s -u admin:password -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/toolbox/runs \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"tool": "json.validate", "input": {"text": "{\"a\": 1}"}}'
+
+
+
+{
+  "run_id": "0f0c...",
+  "tool": "json.validate",
+  "tool_version": "1.0.0",
+  "status": "completed",
+  "outcome": "pass",
+  "summary": {"info": 0, "warning": 0, "error": 0},
+  "findings": [],
+  "output": {"valid": true, "value": {"a": 1}},
+  "duration_ms": 1
+}
+
+
+Invalid JSON returns HTTP 200 with `outcome: "fail"` and a `JSON_INVALID_SYNTAX`
+finding carrying the line/column/character position.
+
+### Diff two strings
+
+bash
+curl -s -u admin:password -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/toolbox/runs \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"tool": "text.diff", "input": {"left": "a\nb\n", "right": "a\nc\n", "context_lines": 3}}'
+
+
+### Inspect a Kubernetes manifest
+
+bash
+curl -s -u admin:password -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/toolbox/runs \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{"tool": "k8s.manifest.inspect", "input": {"manifest": "apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: example\nspec:\n  template:\n    spec:\n      containers:\n        - name: app\n          image: nginx:latest\n          securityContext:\n            privileged: true\n"}}'
+
+
+### Without credentials
+
+bash
+curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:8000/api/toolbox/tools
+# 401
+
+
+## Reference
+
+### Endpoints
+
+| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
+|--------|------|------|-------------|
+| GET | `/api/toolbox/tools` | Basic | Catalog: `id`, `description`, `version`, `input_schema` (JSON Schema) per tool. |
+| POST | `/api/toolbox/runs` | Basic | Run one tool synchronously; returns HTTP 200 with the result and a `run_id`. |
+
+The prefix is `/api/toolbox`, matching the repository's flat convention
+(`/api/debug`, `/api/mgmt`), not the literal `/api/v1/toolbox` of the change
+request.
+
+### HTTP status codes
+
+| Status | Meaning | Body |
+|--------|---------|------|
+| 200 | Run completed (findings may still be present) | `ToolRunResponse` |
+| 401 | Missing/invalid Basic Auth | FastAPI/`app.auth` envelope |
+| 404 | Unknown tool id | `{"error": "Unknown tool", "detail": "<id>"}` |
+| 413 | A configured limit was exceeded | `{"error": "Input exceeds limit", "detail": "<limit>: <observed> > <maximum>"}` |
+| 422 | Body malformed, or payload does not match the tool input schema | FastAPI validation envelope, or `{"error": "Invalid tool input", "detail": [...]}` |
+| 500 | Unexpected internal error | `{"error": "Internal server error", "detail": "run_id=<uuid>"}` |
+| 504 | Run exceeded `TOOLBOX_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `{"error": "Tool run timed out", "detail": "timeout_seconds: <n>"}` |
+
+404/413/504 are returned as explicit `JSONResponse` objects rather than raised, so
+the app-wide 400/404 handlers cannot collapse them into the generic
+`{"error": "Bad request"}` / `{"error": "Not found"}` envelopes.
+
+### Configuration and limits
+
+All limits are env-driven (`app/config/settings.py`) and documented in
+`.env.example`. Exceeding a limit is a controlled 413 that names the limit; inputs
+are **never silently truncated**.
+
+| Variable | Default | Applies to |
+|----------|---------|------------|
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_INPUT_BYTES` | 262144 | `json.validate` (text), `text.diff` (left+right), `k8s.manifest.inspect` (manifest) |
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_YAML_DOCUMENTS` | 50 | `k8s.manifest.inspect` |
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_YAML_DEPTH` | 50 | `k8s.manifest.inspect` (enforced during composition and on the composed graph) |
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_YAML_ALIASES` | 100 | `k8s.manifest.inspect` (anchor/alias expansion budget) |
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_FINDINGS` | 500 | all tools |
+| `TOOLBOX_MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES` | 10 | `text.diff` (`context_lines`; the published schema also caps it at 50) |
+| `TOOLBOX_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 10 | all tools (wall-clock timeout of the worker-thread run) |
+
+#### `text.diff` `context_lines`: published schema vs effective limit
+
+The catalog publishes the tool's JSON Schema, which caps `context_lines` at 50
+(`MAX_CONTEXT_LINES` in `app/toolbox/tools/text_diff.py`). The **effective**
+maximum is the configured `TOOLBOX_MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES` (default 10), enforced
+at run time. A value that is valid per the published schema but above the
+configured limit — for example `context_lines: 20` with the default configuration
+— is rejected with HTTP 413 naming `max_diff_context_lines`; it is **not**
+silently clamped. Raise `TOOLBOX_MAX_DIFF_CONTEXT_LINES` (up to 50) if a larger
+context is needed.
+
+### Finding codes
+
+`json.validate`
+
+| Code | Severity | Category |
+|------|----------|----------|
+| `JSON_EMPTY_INPUT` | error | informational |
+| `JSON_INVALID_SYNTAX` | error | informational |
+
+`text.diff`
+
+| Code | Severity | Category |
+|------|----------|----------|
+| `TEXT_DIFF_DIFFERENT` | info | informational |
+
+`k8s.manifest.inspect`
+
+| Code | Severity | Category |
+|------|----------|----------|
+| `K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_REQUESTS` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_LIMITS` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_MISSING_READINESS_PROBE` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_MISSING_LIVENESS_PROBE` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_IMAGE_MISSING` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_IMAGE_NO_TAG` | warning | risky_configuration |
+| `K8S_IMAGE_LATEST_TAG` | warning | risky_configuration |
+| `K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER` | error | risky_configuration |
+| `K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_ENABLED` | error | risky_configuration |
+| `K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_NOT_DISABLED` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_RUN_AS_ROOT_ALLOWED` | error | risky_configuration |
+| `K8S_RUN_AS_NON_ROOT_NOT_REQUIRED` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_MISSING_POD_SPEC` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_NO_CONTAINERS` | warning | missing_configuration |
+| `K8S_DOCUMENT_NOT_MAPPING` | warning | informational |
+| `K8S_CONTAINER_NOT_MAPPING` | warning | informational |
+| `K8S_UNSUPPORTED_KIND` | info | informational |
+| `K8S_INVALID_YAML` | error | informational |
+
+Router-level
+
+| Code | Severity | Category |
+|------|----------|----------|
+| `TOOL_INPUT_ERROR` | error | informational |
+
+`missing_configuration` means a setting is absent; `risky_configuration` means a
+setting is present and explicitly unsafe. The two are never conflated.
+
+## How-to — adding a new tool
+
+1. Create `app/toolbox/tools/<name>.py` with:
+   - a Pydantic `BaseModel` describing the tool input (this becomes the published
+     `input_schema`);
+   - a class exposing `id`, `version`, `description`, `input_model` and
+     `run(payload, limits) -> ToolResult`.
+   The module must not import FastAPI.
+2. Register the instance in `app/toolbox/registry.py` by adding it to the tuple
+   iterated at import time. Identifiers must be unique; a duplicate fails fast at
+   import.
+3. Add unit tests under `tests/` (valid, invalid, empty, limits, deterministic
+   output) and, if the tool is reachable through the API, an API test.
+4. Document the tool and its finding codes in this file.
+
+## Limitations of the Kubernetes checks
+
+`k8s.manifest.inspect` is a **heuristic static check over the manifest text that
+was supplied**. It is **neither a complete Kubernetes validation nor a security
+certification**. Specifically:
+
+- No API server, admission controller, policy engine or cluster state is
+  consulted; the tool never makes a network call.
+- Only `Deployment`, `StatefulSet` and `DaemonSet` are inspected. Other kinds
+  produce an informational `K8S_UNSUPPORTED_KIND` finding and are skipped.
+- The checks are syntactic: they look for the presence/absence of fields, not for
+  whether the values are semantically valid for a given cluster version.
+- `runAsNonRoot` is evaluated at container level first, then pod level; other
+  non-root mechanisms (for example a non-zero `runAsUser` without
+  `runAsNonRoot: true`) are not treated as satisfying the check.
+- Init containers are inspected for resources, image and securityContext, but
+  probe checks are not applied to them (they run to completion).
+- The tool does not detect every risky configuration; a clean result is not proof
+  that a manifest is safe.
+
+## Architecture note
+
+- **Layout.** `app/toolbox/base.py` holds the pure-Python contracts (a `Tool`
+  `Protocol`, a frozen `ToolLimits` dataclass, `Finding`/`ToolResult` dataclasses,
+  `ToolInputError`/`ToolLimitExceeded`). `app/toolbox/registry.py` is an explicit
+  import-time registry. `app/toolbox/tools/*.py` are the implementations.
+  `app/models/toolbox.py` is the wire contract. `app/routers/toolbox.py` is a thin
+  HTTP layer. Analysis functions never import FastAPI and are unit-testable in
+  isolation.
+- **Execution model.** CPU-bound parsing is dispatched with
+  `loop.run_in_executor`, the same pattern `/api/fib/{x}` already uses, wrapped in
+  `asyncio.wait_for` with a configurable timeout, so the event loop is not blocked.
+- **YAML safety.** Parsing uses a `yaml.SafeLoader` subclass that enforces a
+  composition-depth budget and an alias/anchor budget *during* composition, plus a
+  cycle-aware depth walk over the composed graph. No arbitrary object is ever
+  constructed.
+- **Observability.** The existing loguru setup is reused; the run emits one
+  structured line with `run_id`, `tool`, `status`, `outcome` and `duration_ms` and
+  never logs payloads, manifests, diffs or secrets. Tracing and metrics reuse the
+  existing OpenTelemetry and prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator wiring; no parallel
+  stack and no new metric families are added, and `run_id`/payload/resource names
+  are never used as metric labels.
+
+### Alternatives ruled out
+
+- **A separate service or a queue.** The checks are local, bounded and
+  synchronous; a broker or worker would add infrastructure with no demonstrable
+  need.
+- **A plugin system with dynamic imports.** The registry is explicit and fixed at
+  import time; client input never selects code to import or execute.
+- **Persisting runs / `GET /runs/{id}`.** There is no real persistence system for
+  runs, and an in-memory store pretending to be durable was rejected. `run_id` is
+  correlation-only.
+- **A URL/path heuristic in `json.validate`.** The input schema has a single
+  free-text field, so nothing is dereferenced; the tool parses the string as-is.

+"""Unit tests for the k8s.manifest.inspect tool.
+
+These tests exercise the pure analysis function directly (no FastAPI, no HTTP).
+The tool is heuristic and offline: it never contacts a cluster.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from app.toolbox.base import ToolLimitExceeded, ToolLimits
+from app.toolbox.tools.k8s_manifest import K8sManifestInspectTool, K8sManifestInput
+
+
+def _limits(**overrides) -> ToolLimits:
+    base = dict(
+        max_input_bytes=200000,
+        max_yaml_documents=50,
+        max_yaml_depth=30,
+        max_yaml_aliases=50,
+        max_findings=500,
+        max_diff_context_lines=10,
+    )
+    base.update(overrides)
+    return ToolLimits(**base)
+
+
+def _run(manifest: str, **overrides):
+    tool = K8sManifestInspectTool()
+    return tool.run(K8sManifestInput(manifest=manifest), _limits(**overrides))
+
+
+def _codes(result) -> list[str]:
+    return [f.code for f in result.findings]
+
+
+DEPLOYMENT = (
+    "apiVersion: apps/v1\n"
+    "kind: Deployment\n"
+    "metadata:\n"
+    "  name: example\n"
+    "spec:\n"
+    "  template:\n"
+    "    spec:\n"
+    "      containers:\n"
+    "      - name: app\n"
+    "        image: nginx:1.25\n"
+)
+
+
+def _deployment_with(container_extra: str = "", pod_extra: str = "", init: str = "") -> str:
+    return (
+        "apiVersion: apps/v1\n"
+        "kind: Deployment\n"
+        "metadata:\n"
+        "  name: example\n"
+        "spec:\n"
+        "  template:\n"
+        "    spec:\n"
+        + pod_extra
+        + "      containers:\n"
+        "      - name: app\n"
+        "        image: nginx:1.25\n"
+        + container_extra
+        + init
+    )
+
+
+# --- structure -------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_multi_document_manifest():
+    manifest = DEPLOYMENT + "---\n" + DEPLOYMENT.replace("Deployment", "StatefulSet")
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert result.output["documents"] == 2
+    assert result.output["containers_checked"] == 2
+
+
+def test_empty_documents_are_counted():
+    result = _run("---\n---\n")
+    assert result.output["empty_documents"] >= 1
+
+
+def test_unsupported_kind_is_informational():
+    manifest = "apiVersion: v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n  name: svc\n"
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_UNSUPPORTED_KIND" in _codes(result)
+    finding = next(f for f in result.findings if f.code == "K8S_UNSUPPORTED_KIND")
+    assert finding.severity == "info"
+
+
+def test_document_not_mapping():
+    result = _run("- just\n- a\n- list\n")
+    assert "K8S_DOCUMENT_NOT_MAPPING" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_missing_pod_spec():
+    manifest = "apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: d\nspec: {}\n"
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_POD_SPEC" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_no_containers():
+    manifest = (
+        "apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: d\n"
+        "spec:\n  template:\n    spec:\n      containers: []\n"
+    )
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_NO_CONTAINERS" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_statefulset_and_daemonset_supported():
+    for kind in ("StatefulSet", "DaemonSet"):
+        manifest = DEPLOYMENT.replace("Deployment", kind)
+        result = _run(manifest)
+        assert result.output["containers_checked"] == 1
+
+
+# --- resources -------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_missing_resources():
+    result = _run(DEPLOYMENT)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_REQUESTS" in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_LIMITS" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_resources_present_are_not_reported():
+    extra = (
+        "        resources:\n"
+        "          requests:\n            cpu: 100m\n            memory: 64Mi\n"
+        "          limits:\n            cpu: 200m\n            memory: 128Mi\n"
+    )
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(container_extra=extra))
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_REQUESTS" not in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_RESOURCE_LIMITS" not in _codes(result)
+
+
+# --- probes ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_missing_probes():
+    result = _run(DEPLOYMENT)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_READINESS_PROBE" in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_MISSING_LIVENESS_PROBE" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_init_container_has_no_probe_findings():
+    init = (
+        "      initContainers:\n"
+        "      - name: init\n"
+        "        image: busybox:1.36\n"
+    )
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(init=init))
+    init_findings = [
+        f for f in result.findings if "initContainers" in (f.location.get("path") or "")
+    ]
+    assert init_findings, "init container should still be inspected"
+    assert not any(
+        f.code in ("K8S_MISSING_READINESS_PROBE", "K8S_MISSING_LIVENESS_PROBE")
+        for f in init_findings
+    )
+
+
+# --- images ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_image_without_tag():
+    manifest = DEPLOYMENT.replace("nginx:1.25", "nginx")
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_NO_TAG" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_image_latest_tag():
+    manifest = DEPLOYMENT.replace("nginx:1.25", "nginx:latest")
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_LATEST_TAG" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_image_with_tag_is_clean():
+    result = _run(DEPLOYMENT)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_NO_TAG" not in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_LATEST_TAG" not in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_image_by_digest_is_clean():
+    manifest = DEPLOYMENT.replace(
+        "nginx:1.25", "nginx@sha256:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
+    )
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_NO_TAG" not in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_IMAGE_LATEST_TAG" not in _codes(result)
+
+
+# --- securityContext -------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_privileged_container_is_error():
+    extra = "        securityContext:\n          privileged: true\n"
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(container_extra=extra))
+    assert "K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER" in _codes(result)
+    finding = next(f for f in result.findings if f.code == "K8S_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER")
+    assert finding.severity == "error"
+    assert finding.category == "risky_configuration"
+
+
+def test_allow_privilege_escalation_not_disabled():
+    result = _run(DEPLOYMENT)
+    assert "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_NOT_DISABLED" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_allow_privilege_escalation_enabled_is_error():
+    extra = "        securityContext:\n          allowPrivilegeEscalation: true\n"
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(container_extra=extra))
+    assert "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_ENABLED" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_allow_privilege_escalation_false_is_clean():
+    extra = "        securityContext:\n          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false\n"
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(container_extra=extra))
+    assert "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_NOT_DISABLED" not in _codes(result)
+    assert "K8S_ALLOW_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_ENABLED" not in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_pod_level_run_as_non_root_satisfies_container():
+    pod_extra = "      securityContext:\n        runAsNonRoot: true\n"
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(pod_extra=pod_extra))
+    assert "K8S_RUN_AS_NON_ROOT_NOT_REQUIRED" not in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_run_as_root_allowed_is_error():
+    extra = "        securityContext:\n          runAsNonRoot: false\n"
+    result = _run(_deployment_with(container_extra=extra))
+    assert "K8S_RUN_AS_ROOT_ALLOWED" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_non_root_not_required_is_warning():
+    result = _run(DEPLOYMENT)
+    assert "K8S_RUN_AS_NON_ROOT_NOT_REQUIRED" in _codes(result)
+    finding = next(f for f in result.findings if f.code == "K8S_RUN_AS_NON_ROOT_NOT_REQUIRED")
+    assert finding.severity == "warning"
+    assert finding.category == "missing_configuration"
+
+
+# --- YAML safety -----------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_invalid_yaml_is_reported():
+    result = _run("kind: [unclosed\n")
+    assert "K8S_INVALID_YAML" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_unsafe_yaml_tag_is_rejected():
+    manifest = "!!python/object/apply:os.system ['echo hi']\n"
+    result = _run(manifest)
+    assert "K8S_INVALID_YAML" in _codes(result)
+
+
+def test_alias_budget_is_enforced():
+    manifest = (
+        "a: &a [x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x]\n"
+        "b: &b [*a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a]\n"
+        "c: &c [*b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b]\n"
+        "d: [*c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c, *c]\n"
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ToolLimitExceeded) as exc:
+        _run(manifest, max_yaml_aliases=5)
+    assert exc.value.limit == "max_yaml_aliases"
+
+
+def test_depth_budget_is_enforced():
+    manifest = "a: " + "[" * 100 + "]" * 100 + "\n"
+    with pytest.raises(ToolLimitExceeded) as exc:
+        _run(manifest, max_yaml_depth=10)
+    assert exc.value.limit == "max_yaml_depth"
+
+
+# --- limits ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_input_size_budget_is_enforced():
+    manifest = "kind: Service\n" + "# pad\n" * 1000
+    with pytest.raises(ToolLimitExceeded) as exc:
+        _run(manifest, max_input_bytes=10)
+    assert exc.value.limit == "max_input_bytes"
+
+
+def test_document_budget_is_enforced():
+    manifest = "\n---\n".join(["kind: Service"] * 5)
+    with pytest.raises(ToolLimitExceeded) as exc:
+        _run(manifest, max_yaml_documents=2)
+    assert exc.value.limit == "max_yaml_documents"
+
+
+def test_findings_budget_is_enforced():
+    containers = "\n".join(
+        f"      - name: c{i}\n        image: nginx" for i in range(20)
+    )
+    manifest = (
+        "apiVersion: apps/v1\nkind: Deployment\nmetadata:\n  name: d\n"
+        "spec:\n  template:\n    spec:\n      containers:\n" + containers + "\n"
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ToolLimitExceeded) as exc:
+        _run(manifest, max_findings=5)
+    assert exc.value.limit == "max_findings"
+
+
+# --- determinism / honesty -------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_output_is_deterministic():
+    manifest = _deployment_with(
+        container_extra="        securityContext:\n          privileged: true\n"
+    )
+    first = _run(manifest)
+    second = _run(manifest)
+    assert _codes(first) == _codes(second)
+    assert first.output == second.output
+
+
+def test_disclaimer_is_present():
